findings.title: No affected-row verification for delete
findings.description: The mapper exposes only the implicit affected-row count; there is no guard against a 0-row delete (for example, an already-deleted company or a mismatched COMPANY_STATE). Callers must verify the returned count. Static observation; runtime behavior unverified.
findings.recommendation: Check the affected-row count in the service layer and roll back or raise when it is 0.

findings.title: State-conditioned delete guard
findings.description: Including COMPANY_STATE in the WHERE clause acts as a guard that prevents deleting a company in an unexpected state. Combined with ID, this is a reasonable data-safety pattern. Static observation; no runtime evidence collected.
findings.recommendation: Retain the state guard and document it as an intentional idempotency/data-safety control.

findings.title: Null parameter binding semantics
findings.description: A null id or companyState resolves to '= NULL' and deletes zero rows silently instead of failing. If a delete with missing parameters must be rejected, validation belongs in the service layer. Static observation; unverified at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Validate that id and companyState are non-null before invoking the mapper to avoid a silently successful no-op delete.
